Stated Claim / Post Context:
Call on the Federal Government to end the free ride for fossil fuels! - Climate Council

Join our call for Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and key Federal Ministers to stand up to fossil fuel corporations and protect the interests of all Australians

Actual Article Body:
Growing a bigger, cleaner energy grid.

How we make things matters.

Cleaner, cheaper and better transport choices.

Take Action

/

Climate Politics

Meanwhile, the rest of us are left footing the bill for the climate damage.

Higher insurance premiums, spiralling costs for imported fuel, and billions in disaster recovery from worsening fires, floods and heatwaves are among the costs we pay for fossil fuel pollution, and they hit harder every year.

But while everyday Australians tighten their belts, highly polluting coal, oil and gas corporations are raking in record profits and pocketing billions in government subsidies, leaving everyday Australians to pick up the tab for the climate damage.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Albanese says AI government website hack a 'wake-up call'

The timing of this revelation was "pretty tactical" according to Olivia Shen, a Director at the United States Studies Centre at the University of Sydney.

Actual Article Body:
Anthony Albanese made the revelation after a call with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. (Source: 1News)

SHARE ME

The first reported artificial intelligence agent hack into an Australian government website is a "wake-up call" of the dangers of the technology, Anthony Albanese says.

The prime minister revealed at a press conference in New York this week that an OpenAI agent scaled a digital "fence" to breach a Medicare platform and access non-public information.

Staff had only directed it to research public medicine funding on the internet.

Jacob Coxon says the race to build ever-more powerful systems is moving faster than the safeguards needed to control them.  (Source: 1News)

Speaking to former prime minister Kevin Rudd, who now heads up the Asia Society, Albanese said the hack was cause for concern about whether "humans remain in charge".
